title: A written rubric plus independent double labeling raises agreement enough to measure capability on implementation classification
summary: If 'implemented / partial / missing' is defined by an explicit rubric (for example: partial = code at the base implements at least one named component of the proposed change, cited by symbol) and labels come from two independent labelers with adjudication, inter-sample agreement and cheap-route accuracy rise toward >= 0.9. Deprioritized (FND-0005): the family is a rare meta-task, so qualifying a route for it has low downstream value; prefer recurring task families with deterministic labels first.

provenance.author_tier: frontier (Opus 5.5) analysis of deterministic eval output
